summary: Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas and former Republican Sen. John E. Sununu are fighting for the open seat left by Jeanne Shaheen, and WGME reported in mid October that recent polls showed Pappas ahead by seven to eight points after a closer September. Pappas ties Sununu to Trump, the Iran war and tariffs, while Sununu argues Pappas has accomplished little in eight years in Washington.

issues.why: Pappas says the economy is rigged for billionaires and blames Trump's tariffs for rising costs, while Sununu says Pappas has not delivered for the state.
Sununu has voiced disagreement with the Iran war and the trade war with Canada as Democrats call him Trump's hand picked candidate.
The Pappas campaign says Sununu backed health care cuts and once proposed privatizing Social Security.
Sununu says New Hampshire is last in New England in highway funding, and Pappas points to his Highway Fair Share Act.
Pappas makes building more homes and child care his priorities in a state with tight housing.

storylines.title: Sununu skips Dartmouth forum
storylines.what: NHPR canceled its Oct. 29 Senate forum in Hanover after Sununu declined, citing his schedule, leaving the WMUR debate on Oct. 28.

storylines.title: Closing pitches
storylines.what: Sununu says Pappas has attempted very little and accomplished even less, while Pappas calls Sununu a failed politician from the past.

storylines.title: Salem chamber forum
storylines.what: The two met at a Southern New Hampshire Chamber of Commerce forum in Salem a day after their first debate.

storylines.title: First debate in Conway
storylines.what: The Pappas campaign says Sununu ran from his past remark that the race matters to Trump's agenda and would not detail Social Security changes.

storylines.title: Pappas lead grows in polls
storylines.what: Recent polls show Pappas up seven to eight points after a two point edge a month earlier, with about $50 million spent so far.

storylines.title: SLF ad calls Pappas insider
storylines.what: Senate Leadership Fund argues Pappas voted on bills his partner lobbied on and calls him a corrupt political insider.

storylines.title: Trump aligned PAC reserves $10 million
storylines.what: No Going Back PAC, backed by MAGA Inc., reserved about $10 million in ads to elect Sununu.

storylines.title: Race moves to toss up
storylines.what: Cook shifted the race to toss up as Sununu hit Pappas on highway funding, while Sununu says he has never met Trump.

events.title: Trump's endorsement
events.prompt: Trump has endorsed the Republican, and his approval is negative in New Hampshire while the Iran war and Canada tariffs are unpopular. How does the campaign handle Trump?

opts.label: Make it a referendum
opts.say: Call the race a check on Trump's reckless leadership and back a war powers resolution.

opts.label: Independent voice
opts.say: Break with Trump on tariffs and Iran but say you can work with the administration.

opts.label: Run with Trump
opts.say: Embrace the endorsement and promise to pass the president's agenda.

events.title: Social Security question
events.prompt: At the first debate the Republican would not lay out specific Social Security changes, and Democrats say he once proposed privatizing it. How does the campaign answer?

opts.label: No cuts, expand it
opts.say: Pledge no benefit cuts and lift the payroll cap on high earners.

opts.label: Bipartisan commission
opts.say: Promise to protect current retirees and back a bipartisan solvency deal.

opts.label: Reform for the young
opts.say: Argue the program needs structural reform and personal accounts for younger workers.

events.title: Lobbying attacks
events.prompt: Ads from both sides center on lobbying, one saying the Democrat voted on bills his partner lobbied on and another saying the Republican cashed in at lobbying firms. How does the campaign respond?

opts.label: Ban stock and lobby ties
opts.say: Back a ban on members trading stock and a lifetime lobbying ban.

opts.label: Release records
opts.say: Release ethics and client records and challenge the other side to do the same.

opts.label: Hit the insider
opts.say: Call the opponent a creature of Washington who has delivered nothing.

events.title: Highway funding gap
events.prompt: New Hampshire gets some of the lowest federal road funding per person in the country, and both candidates are claiming the issue. What is the campaign's pitch?

opts.label: Fair share mandate
opts.say: Push a guaranteed floor of federal highway money for small states.

opts.label: Seniority pitch
opts.say: Argue a Senate majority seat will deliver more road money to the state.

opts.label: Blame the incumbent
opts.say: Say eight years in Congress produced no new roads money.

debates.where: Conway, Mount Washington Valley Economic Council

endorsements.who: Don Bolduc, former GOP Senate nominee

ads.theme: Calls Pappas a corrupt insider who voted on bills his partner lobbied on.
A MAGA Inc. backed group reserved about $10 million to elect Sununu.
Ads say Sununu cashed in by working for lobbying firms after leaving the Senate.

regions.note: Pappas's 1st District base, where Democratic Portsmouth and Dover offset Republican Salem and border towns.

regions.name: Concord and the Lakes Region
regions.note: Democratic leaning Concord next to the reliably Republican Lakes Region.

regions.note: Dartmouth and Keene anchor a Democratic leaning west side of the state.

regions.note: Rural, older and increasingly Republican, with tourism towns around Conway.
